name: Google Maps
purpose: Navigation, transit directions, opening hours, offline areas
notes: Download the Tokyo area for offline use before you arrive. Transit directions are surprisingly accurate and include platform exits.

name: Google Translate
purpose: Menu & sign translation (camera mode), voice conversations
notes: Download Japanese offline. Camera mode reads kanji menus in real time; conversation mode handles spoken exchanges.

name: Suica (Apple Wallet) / Mobile Suica
purpose: Tap-to-pay for trains, buses, convenience stores
notes: On iPhone 8 or later, add a Suica inside Apple Wallet and top up with Apple Pay. Saves the hassle of buying a physical card.

name: Japan Travel by NAVITIME
purpose: Offline train timetables, JR Pass route planner, station exit guide
notes: Tourist-focused. Free tier is generous; premium unlocks offline maps. Excellent for Shinkansen planning.

name: GO — Japan's #1 Taxi App
purpose: Hailing licensed taxis in Tokyo and 40+ other cities
notes: Uber in Tokyo is very limited; GO is the reliable default. Pays the metered fare, not surge.

name: LINE
purpose: Messaging (the dominant app in Japan), some business bookings
notes: Many small businesses, tour operators, and locals prefer LINE over email. Useful for coordinating with guides or homestays.

name: Tabelog
purpose: Real local restaurant reviews and ratings
notes: A 3.5+ on Tabelog is strong; 3.8+ is excellent. Skews pickier than Google. Some reservations require a Japanese phone number.

name: NERV Disaster Prevention
purpose: Earthquake early warnings, tsunami & typhoon alerts (English UI)
notes: Fast, clean, English-friendly version of the national JMA alerts. Install before you land.

name: Japan Official Travel App (JNTO)
purpose: Free Wi-Fi finder, ATM locator, tax-free shop map
notes: Decent offline basics. The Wi-Fi finder and tax-free map are the killer features.

name: Ecbo Cloak
purpose: Book luggage storage at cafés, shops, and hotels city-wide
notes: Often cheaper and easier than coin lockers, which fill up at popular stations by mid-morning.

name: Uber / Uber Eats
purpose: Food delivery (works as a tourist) + limited ride-hail
notes: Uber Eats Japan accepts foreign cards and English addresses. For taxis use GO — Uber ride-hail itself is sparse in Tokyo.

name: Demae-can (出前館)
notes: Bigger restaurant catalogue than Uber Eats in Japan, including local chains (Yoshinoya, Coco Ichibanya, Hotto Motto bentos). UI is Japanese-first — pair with Google Translate.

name: Wolt
purpose: Premium food + groceries delivery (Finnish, widely-trusted English UI)
notes: English-first UI, reliable for hotel-room delivery. Covers central wards in Tokyo, Yokohama, Osaka and a handful of other cities.

name: menu
purpose: Food delivery with strong coverage in outer Tokyo wards
notes: Japanese-owned, fills gaps where Uber Eats and Wolt don't deliver. Useful once you're past Shibuya / Shinjuku into residential areas.

name: Amazon.co.jp
notes: Set the language to English in Settings. Prime same-day works across Tokyo; Amazon Fresh handles groceries in central wards. Foreign cards accepted.

name: Rakuten Seiyu Netsuper
notes: Cheaper grocery baseline than Amazon. Requires a Rakuten account — setup is in Japanese but Google Translate handles it.

name: DiDi
notes: Strong in Osaka and Kyoto; thinner in Tokyo outside Shinjuku / Roppongi. Occasionally cheaper than GO via promo codes.

name: S.RIDE
notes: Launched by Sony + local operators. Fast pickups in central Tokyo, no surge pricing.

name: Yamato Takuhaibin
purpose: Forward heavy luggage between hotels overnight
notes: Not an app per se — ask at your hotel front desk or a konbini. Typical suitcase forwarding is ¥2,000-¥2,500 and saves you lugging suitcases on crowded trains.
